issue_context.title: Rename the `newTabPosition` strings
issue_context.body:
Follow-up from #13421

### Settings UI
Position of the new tab --> Position of newly created tabs
Specifies position of the new tab --> Specifies where new tabs appear in the tab row
At the end --> After the last tab
After current tab	--> After the current tab

### JSON
atTheEnd --> afterLastTab
afterCurrentTab --> afterCurrentTab

No need for legacy converter

### Code
we _should_ rename the enums to match the new names
comments: Is this a legacy converter? It doesn't compile for me without it. https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/6c2316df44779deb9480c769e3354187660e6736/src/cascadia/TerminalSettingsModel/TerminalSettingsSerializationHelpers.h#L240-L246
Sorry, we didn't make that super clear. A legacy converter is one that includes support for the old data that might be in a user's settings file :smile:

:tada:This issue was addressed in #13602, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v1.16.252`.:tada:

review_comments:
We should keep an `atTheEnd` entry here to ensure that existing users' settings still work:
```cpp
pair_type{ "atTheEnd", ValueType::AfterLastTab },
```

We can ensure that `afterLastTab` is preferred over `atTheEnd` by putting that legacy mapping after the new one (for instance at the end of the list).
Is that what "No need for legacy converter" in the issue was about?
Oh, yeah, we don't need to include the legacy value at all -- this feature didn't ship outside of limited selfhost!
